rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Turn 3 Build 4 Improve 5 Deliver 6 Take 7 Scoring Overview The aim is to have the largest network, largest train, and most deliveries when three or more cities are depleted of cubes Turn After the dice are rolled, pick a dice face and take an action with it, these are: Build Improve Deliver Take Order (Expansion) Build Draw a line of track in the corresponding region e.g. yellow for a 1 dice, and the angle of the curve is based on the back dice shape (two options are provided) Any space (except the dice spaces) can be drawn in, regardless of previous connections or lack of e.g. you can place two unconnected lines in red, or a line in yellow and a line in green on separate turns Improve Cross off a box in no particular order to increase the size of your train, each crossed off box gives you +1 size the size is how many towns/cities you can pass through when trying to make a delivery Deliver The dice chosen is the start city for loading goods and the good shows the colour of the city it wants to be delivered to, you must have a continuous connection between the two cities and a size equal or exceeding the number of towns and cities you have to pass through including the destination Each town or city passed through (including the destination city) gives 1 point, so the longer the route to reach the destination, the more points you will gain for the delivery Take Take an upright action tile matching the number of the dice and turn it sideways, this can be a neutral one, an opponent's one, or your own. Taking your own stops an opponent potentially taking it as it will again be turned sideways and locked off for now. There are two main types, one off and continuous. A one off tile will be discarded back to the neutral area once it is used, whilst a continuous one will provide its benefit to you as long as you own it Warning, some tiles will lose you points at game's end Scoring In addition to during game points of delivery lengths, you also gain points for: 2 points per city to city connection, +1 point per town crossed as part of the connection (towns crossed but not connecting two cities score nothing) Train size of 4+ will score 1 point per size at or above this Tiles may give or lose you points if you still hold them

[Rating: 2/10] Ruled not so good. Some turns basically had nothing to do.  Better option available.

[Rating: 2/10] Years ago, I attempted to make an Age of Steam Express game. It didn't come out very well. SteamRollers goes to show that there's really no such thing as an Age of Steam dice game that works very well. This is way too long, way too random, and just not that interesting.

[Rating: 3/10] A Steam-style train roll-and-write, SteamRollers has players building tracks to connect cities to deliver goods in the same manner as the Steam series--more of a connect to deliver as opposed to a pick up and deliver. Playing this one though, is not near as fun as its inspiration. It starts a bit too slow, and because each player is working their own mat, there is no competition between laying tracks to see who benefits from connecting cities/goods. The game ramps us a bit part-way through once routes begin to develop, but the other addition, ability cards, are a bit unwieldy and feel somewhat

[Rating: 3/10] The most I’ve ever been disappointed in the quality of the components. I paid $32 dollars new for a small game with all very thin warped boards and other cardboard components, and cheap looking art and components all around. The game itself seemed like it didn’t know what it wanted to be so it lets you figure that out by piecing together the rules and components you do like. In the end it was a total failure for us and was neither fun as a train game nor as a roll and write.

[Rating: 3/10] Route building repackaged as a roll and write. With the special power tiles, dice selection, and turn order binding, there's some hints of Steam's combination of route building and role selection. Unfortunately, the implementation manages to up the tedium via incremental turns; adds a layer, via the dice, that results in players having less control; lessens legibility via the separated player boards; and provides little to no leeching of opponents' efforts. Why are we playing this again and not any of the other Steam or Winsome-related titles? Poor; quite poor.

[Rating: 3/10] Just the blandest mash up of a pick up and deliver train game and a Roll and Write, executed with literally nothing exciting about it. Rough.

[Rating: 3/10] What a boring game, probably the least interesting roll & write I've ever played. Please do not judge the quality of mechanisms in the "real" Age of Steam / Steam after playing this one.
